sources.note: Catalogue pages: SIL lists exactly one item for Toura (Kassell & Potter 2011); GlottologGlottolog's fullest description is only a wordlist, 0 descriptive refs; Wikipedia stub notes PARADISEC audio collections only.

sources.citation: Hammarstrom, Harald & Sebastian Nordhoff. 2012. Online appendix to 'The languages of Melanesia: quantifying the level of coverage'. In Nicholas Evans & Marian Klamer (eds.), Melanesian languages on the edge of Asia: challenges for the 21st century (Language Documentation & Conservation Special Publication 5), 13-34. Honolulu: University of Hawai'i Press. hdl:10125/4559 (appendix PDF, c. 950 pp.)
sources.source_kind: database or survey citing another work
sources.note: Melanesia-wide coverage bibliography (one entry per language listing its most extensive descriptive sources with type tags); entry lists only Kassell & Potter 2011 Abadi ESR 2011-030 [wordlist, socling]; Pawley 1975 (PL C-29) [comparative]; no phonology or grammar recorded for this language and no stress or tone content anywhere in the entry.

sources.citation: Kassell, Alison and Margaret Potter. 2011. A sociolinguistic profile of the Abadi language group. SIL Electronic Survey Report 2011-030. Dallas: SIL International. 59 pp.
sources.note: Nothing. Survey of Lala, Abadi and Toura (June-July 2003). Sec. 8.1 'Characteristics of the language' lists phones of Abadi only. Appendix A.4 (pp. 53-58) gives two Toura wordlists (Akuku, Toromoku villages) in phonetic transcription with no stress marks (0 occurrences of the IPA stress mark in the text). Only Toura item listed by SIL PNG and the SIL archive for [don].

sources.citation: Lynch, John, Malcolm Ross and Terry Crowley. 2002. The Oceanic languages. Richmond: Curzon. (pp. 54-55)
sources.note: Nothing. Doura mentioned only as a member of the 'Proto B' Central Papuan subgroup (t > k innovation) in the comparative-method illustration; no sketch of Doura.

sources.citation: Dutton, Tom & Darrell T. Tryon (eds). 1994. Language contact and change in the Austronesian world (Trends in Linguistics. Studies and Monographs 77). Berlin/New York: Mouton de Gruyter. ISBN 3-11-012786-5. [Held is the text of the whole 696-page volume although catalogued under Rivierre's chapter 'Contact-induced phonological complexification in New Caledonia', pp. 497-522, DOI 10.1515/9783110883091.497; chapters read for targets: Adelaar 'The classification of the Tamanic languages' 1-42; Bugenhagen 'Language change on Umboi Island' 43-108; Clark 'The Polynesian Outliers as a locus of language contact' 109-139; Dutton 'Motu-Koiarian contact in Papua New Guinea' 181-232; B. D. Grimes 'Cloves and nutmeg..' 251-274; Reid 'Unravelling the linguistic histories of Philippine Negritos' 443-475; Tryon 'Language contact and contact-induced language change in the Eastern Outer Islands, Solomon Islands' 611-648; Voorhoeve '..north Moluccas' 649-674.]
sources.note: No prosodic statement; Doura figures only as a comparison language in consonant-correspondence tables and a loan-source chart. Marginal coverage (table rows, no description).

sources.citation: Ross, Malcolm D. 1994. Central Papuan culture history: some lexical evidence. In A. K. Pawley & M. D. Ross (eds.), Austronesian terminologies: continuity and change (Pacific Linguistics C-127), 389-479. Canberra: ANU.
sources.note: Read the ANU text (searched stress/accent/Doura, read the sound-change discussion around Figure 2): consonant correspondences and loan strata (PCP *t > NWCP *k, Doura kavara 'sea/sand') only; no prosodic information for any language; Doura forms unmarked for stress.
sources.venue: Austronesian terminologies: continuity and change (Pacific Linguistics C-127)

sources.citation: Ross, Malcolm. 1988. Proto Oceanic and the Austronesian languages of western Melanesia (Pacific Linguistics C-98). Canberra: ANU. (Central Papuan section pp. 190-212)
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: open copy online; also held in print at Harvard (Widener Library (offsite storage), call number PL6201.R67 1988)
sources.harvard_location: Widener Library (offsite storage), call number PL6201 .R67 1988
sources.note: Nothing on Doura stress. Doura appears in the Central Papuan consonant-correspondence tables (pp. 192, 205) and cognate sets; data source given as 'Dutton n.d.' (Appendix B). Stress mentions in the book concern other languages (Ali, Yabem area).

sources.citation: Pawley, Andrew. 1976. Austronesian languages: western part of south-eastern mainland Papua. In S. A. Wurm (ed.), New Guinea area languages and language study, vol. 2 (Pacific Linguistics C-39), 301-319. Canberra: ANU.
sources.note: Nothing on stress. p. 301, source list: "DOURA. Spoken by several hundred in three to six villages around the eastern side of Galley Reach. No published grammar or dictionary."
sources.venue: New Guinea area languages and language study

sources.citation: Taylor, A. J. 1976. History of research in Austronesian languages: western part of south-eastern mainland Papua. In S. A. Wurm (ed.), New Guinea area languages and language study, vol. 2: Austronesian languages (Pacific Linguistics C-39), 141-156. Canberra: ANU. (sec. 4.2.6.2 'Doura', p. 144; notes 1 and 7)
sources.note: No phonology content. Research history only: 'This language is spoken by only about 300 people today and has not been studied much. Chalmers collected a wordlist (in Chalmers and McFarlane 1888) and this was the only material available to Ray in 1907, so that he does not include Doura in his discussion of the phonology and grammar of the Melanesian languages of British New Guinea.. In a later paper Ray (1929: 96) refers to vocabulary lists and notes made by Strong and from them he lists the forms of pronouns.. In the last few years Wilson has done some work on the language in connection with…
sources.venue: New Guinea area languages and language study

sources.citation: Pawley, Andrew. 1975. The relationship of the Austronesian languages of Central Papua: a preliminary study. In T. E. Dutton (ed.), Studies in languages of central and south-east Papua (Pacific Linguistics C-29), 3-106. Canberra: ANU.
sources.note: Nothing on Doura stress. Sec. 3.6 Doura (pp. 13-14): 3-6 villages east of Galley Reach; data from Mr Kere Moi (UPNG student, 1969). Rest is comparative sound correspondences and lexicostatistics. The one stress rule in the volume (p. 109, 'Stress is unmarked but always occurs on the first syllable of bisyllabic words and on the second last syllable of words of more than two syllables') belongs to Kolia's Balawaia (Sinaugoro) sketch, not Doura.
sources.venue: Studies in languages of central and south-east Papua (Pacific Linguistics C-29)

sources.citation: Ray, Sidney H. 1929. The languages of the Central Division of Papua. Journal of the Royal Anthropological Institute 59: 65-96.
sources.note: Ray's grammatical notes on Central Division languages sometimes include a line on accent; Doura is among the languages covered (Glottolog: wordlist-level). Now US public domain; HathiTrust full view exists but blocked bot access.
sources.venue: Journal of the Royal Anthropological Institute

sources.citation: Ray, Sidney H. 1907. The Melanesian languages of British New Guinea. In Reports of the Cambridge Anthropological Expedition to Torres Straits, vol. III: Linguistics, 413-503. Cambridge: CUP.
sources.note: Nothing. Doura occurs only in the language/locality list, the numeral table (p. 470) and the comparative vocabulary; Ray's Doura data are 'MS., Rev. J. Chalmers. Printed in British New Guinea Vocabularies, 1889'. No grammatical or phonological notes for Doura; no 'accent'/'stress' lines anywhere in the British New Guinea section.
sources.venue: Reports of the Cambridge Anthropological Expedition to Torres Straits, vol

sources.citation: Greenhill, S. J., Blust, R. & Gray, R. D. (eds.), Austronesian Basic Vocabulary Database, language 396 'Doura'. Source/Author: Malcolm Ross, W.C. Papua list; typed by Janet Moody. 210-item Swadesh-type list (ISO don, glottocode tour1243).
sources.note: Wordlist-only data: c. 150 filled items in practical orthography with glottal stop marked by apostrophe (lauri'u, itipa'u, 'ura, lu'ara); zero stress or accent marks, no notes field content. Not a statement.

sources.citation: Potter, Margaret and Alison Kassell. 2004. Toura language survey report. SIL-PNG unpublished manuscript, 49 pp. (Glottolog 106462)
